key_insight: Large language models can extract semantic concepts from materials-science abstracts to build concept graphs, and a trained predictor can forecast novel, high-potential topic combinations to inspire new research directions.
problem_solved: Identifies and predicts emerging interdisciplinary research topics from historical literature, helping experts discover promising but non-obvious research directions that standard literature search or trend analyses can miss.
method: Use LLMs to extract and normalize semantic concepts and relations from materials-science abstracts.
Construct temporal concept graphs that capture co-occurrence and evolving relationships between concepts.
Train a machine-learning model on historical graph snapshots to predict emerging combinations of concepts and present ranked suggestions to experts.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to combine LLM-based semantic extraction with graph-based temporal prediction for research foresight, accelerating hypothesis generation and targeted exploration in materials science and other domains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: abstracts → LLM concept extraction → concept graph construction → predictive model → suggested topic combinations
Concept graph snapshot with highlighted emerging links (before vs. after) to show predicted new combinations
Timeline/heatmap showing emergence probability of topic pairs over time
Example card: input concepts and a top-ranked suggested new research direction with confidence score
paper_title: Predicting new research directions in materials science using large language models and concept graphs
paper_authors: Thomas Marwitz, Alexander Colsmann, Ben Breitung, Christoph Brabec, Christoph Kirchlechner
